children: Some cryptocurrency assets can count toward the reserves that trading platforms and clearinghouses must keep on hand, but not toward a separate liquidity requirement, staff at the US commodities regulator said in an advisory on Monday.
Staff in the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk issued the advisory.
It applies to swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations.
The advisory addresses three CFTC regulations that require these entities to hold enough financial resources to cover at least 12 months of operating costs.
The staff said bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins may count toward that requirement "subject to appropriate haircuts."
Crypto assets cannot satisfy the separate liquidity requirement because they don't qualify as cash or highly liquid securities under accounting rules, according to the advisory.

CFTC said the advisory only reflects the views of staff and does not create new rules or enforceable rights, is not a no-action position, and does not necessarily represent the views of the commission.
